newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower on fund selling.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower after succumbing to a wave of commodity fund selling that began about 1200 CDT and continued until the close, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures closed lower reflecting declines in the live cattle market.
Led by Refco Inc, which sold at least 1,500 December live cattle contracts, the selling vanquished early gains. Traders said Refco's selling appeared to be long liquidation.

Traders said the selloff may put a lid on cash cattle prices as well. Early Wednesday, analysts and traders said cash cattle may trade at $73.00 per cwt this week, but after the CME close, traders said $72.00 may the high.
"That is old news," said one trader about the $73 forecasts.
Cattle trading has been light at High Plains feedlots this week and USDA on Wednesday reported light sales of lower-quality cattle at $71.00.

Chart-based selling in CME December live cattle began near 66.00 cents a lb and accelerated when stops were triggered near 65.75 cents, traders said. December's low of 65.35 cents attracted light commericial buying that trimmed declines.
Cash beef prices were lower at midday but analysts and traders said technical factors rather than lower beef values appeared to be the reason for selling in cattle futures.

Feeder cattle held gains early but ended lower largely in sympathy with the decline in live cattle futures. Active spread trading occurred in feeder cattle largely October/November, November/October, and buying of May 1997 feeder cattle and selling of October live cattle.

Live cattle closed down 0.600 to 0.200 cent a lb with October off the most at 71.425 cents. Feeder cattle finished off 0.750 to 0.200 cent with October off 0.325 at 63.175 and November was off 0.750 at 63.675.
